claims.text: GINA: adults and adolescents should not be treated with SABA alone
claims.quote: Adults and adolescents with asthma should not be treated with SABA alone.

claims.text: Low-dose ICS-formoterol is the preferred reliever for adolescents and adults
claims.quote: Low-dose ICS-formoterol is the preferred reliever for adolescents and adults

claims.text: Asthma is usually characterized by chronic airway inflammation
claims.quote: usually characterized by chronic airway inflammation.

claims.text: Early low-dose ICS associated with better lung function than starting after more than 2-4 years of symptoms
claims.quote: Early treatment with low-dose ICS is associated with better lung function ... than starting when symptoms have been present for more than 2–4 years.

claims.text: GINA exacerbation risk factors: allergen exposure if sensitized, smoking, vaping, air pollution
claims.quote: Exposure to allergens (if sensitized), smoking, vaping, air pollution

claims.text: Exacerbations often triggered by viral upper respiratory infection
claims.quote: Exacerbations are often triggered by viral upper respiratory tract infection,

claims.text: Allergy features and family history of asthma or allergy are risk factors for persistence of childhood asthma
claims.quote: Risk factors for persistence of childhood asthma include allergy features, a family history of asthma or allergy,

claims.text: Asthma is more difficult to control in people with obesity
claims.quote: Asthma is more difficult to control in people with obesity.

claims.text: Review 1-3 months after starting treatment
claims.quote: asthma should be reviewed 1–3 months after starting treatment, then every 3–12 months

claims.text: Consider stepping down after 3 months or more of good control
claims.quote: If asthma has been well controlled for 3 months or more, consider stepping down.

claims.text: SABA-only treatment associated with exacerbations, worse lung function and asthma death
claims.quote: SABA-only treatment is associated with increased risk of exacerbations, worse lung function ... and increased risk of death due to asthma.

claims.text: All adults, adolescents and children 6-11 should receive ICS-containing treatment
claims.quote: All adults, adolescents and children aged 6–11 years should receive treatment that includes ICS.

claims.text: As-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol reduces emergency visits or hospitalizations by 65% vs SABA alone
claims.quote: Reduces emergency visits/hospitalizations by 65% compared with SABA alone

claims.text: Track 1 Steps 1-2: as-needed low-dose ICS-formoterol
claims.quote: The recommended treatment is low-dose ICS-formoterol taken whenever needed to relieve asthma symptoms.

claims.text: Track 1 Step 3 MART low-dose maintenance ICS-formoterol
claims.quote: MART* with low-dose maintenance ICS-formoterol

claims.text: Track 1 Step 4 MART medium-dose maintenance ICS-formoterol
claims.quote: MART* with medium-dose maintenance ICS-formoterol

claims.text: MART is also called SMART
claims.quote: Maintenance-and-reliever therapy with combination ICS-formoterol (also called SMART)

claims.text: Track 2 is the alternative when ICS-formoterol is not available
claims.quote: This is an alternative approach when ICS-formoterol is not available.

claims.text: Track 2 may be considered with stable asthma and no exacerbations
claims.quote: Track 2 may also be considered if a patient has stable asthma and no exacerbations

claims.text: Track 2 Step 1: no maintenance ICS; take ICS whenever SABA used
claims.quote: No maintenance ICS. If reliever is SABA, take ICS whenever SABA used

claims.text: Track 2 Step 2 low-dose maintenance ICS
claims.quote: Low dose maintenance ICS

claims.text: Track 2 Steps 3 and 4: low-dose then medium-dose maintenance ICS-LABA
claims.quote: Low dose maintenance ICS-LABA ... Medium dose maintenance ICS-LABA

claims.text: Step 5: refer for phenotype, consider high-dose maintenance ICS-formoterol
claims.quote: Refer for assessment of phenotype. Consider trial of high-dose maintenance ICS-formoterol.

claims.text: Step 5: add-on LAMA; consider anti-IgE, anti-IL5/5R, anti-IL4Ra, anti-TSLP
claims.quote: Add-on LAMA ... Consider anti-IgE, anti-IL5/5R, anti-IL4Rα, anti-TSLP

claims.text: Step 5 (Track 2 column): refer for expert assessment, phenotyping and add-on treatment
claims.quote: Refer for expert assessment, phenotyping, and add-on treatment for severe asthma.

claims.text: Every patient should have a written asthma action plan
claims.quote: All patients should have a written asthma action plan.

claims.text: Measure lung function with spirometry or PEF meter
claims.quote: Measure lung function with spirometry (or with a PEF meter, if spirometry is not possible).

claims.text: Bronchodilator reversibility criterion: FEV1 or FVC increase >=12% and >=200 mL (adults)
claims.quote: Adults: FEV1 or FVC increases by ≥12% and by ≥200 mL from the pre-bronchodilator value

claims.text: Symptom control question on night waking
claims.quote: Any night waking due to asthma?

claims.text: Severe exacerbation in past year is a risk factor
claims.quote: Severe exacerbation in past year or lifetime history of intubation or ICU admission for asthma

claims.text: Check adherence, technique, risk factors and comorbidities before stepping up
claims.quote: check adherence, inhaler technique, risk factors and comorbidities first, before stepping up treatment

claims.text: Comorbidities to assess
claims.quote: rhinitis, rhinosinusitis, gastroesophageal reflux disease, obesity, obstructive sleep apnea, or depression and anxiety

claims.text: GERD listed among conditions linked to exacerbation risk
claims.quote: Medical conditions (obesity, chronic rhinosinusitis, GERD, confirmed food allergy) or pregnancy

claims.text: Elevated FeNO >50 ppb in adults/adolescents supports Type 2 asthma
claims.quote: elevated FeNO (adults/adolescents: >50 ppb; children: >35 ppb)

claims.text: Lower FeNO does not rule out asthma
claims.quote: Lower levels of FeNO or blood eosinophils do not rule out asthma.

claims.text: ICS markedly reduce risk of hospitalization and death
claims.quote: ICS-containing medication markedly reduces risk of asthma hospitalizations and death.

claims.text: LABA should not be used without ICS
claims.quote: LABA should not be used without ICS in patients with asthma (or asthma+COPD).

claims.text: Add-on LAMA slightly improves lung function and slightly reduces exacerbations
claims.quote: add-on LAMA slightly improves lung function and slightly reduces the risk of exacerbations

claims.text: Biologic treatment can be added to maximal treatment
claims.quote: Biologic treatment can be added to maximal treatment, if available and affordable.

claims.text: Check inhaler technique at every opportunity
claims.quote: Check inhaler technique at every opportunity.

claims.text: Patients using ICS in a pMDI should use a spacer
claims.quote: Patients using ICS in a pressurized metered-dose inhaler should use a spacer.

claims.text: Exercise as a trigger should not be avoided
claims.quote: such as exercise and laughter, should not be avoided.

claims.text: Low-dose ICS-formoterol can be used before exercise
claims.quote: Patients can also use low-dose ICS-formoterol before exercise or before or during exposure to allergens, if needed.

claims.text: Occupational asthma: ask about allergens or irritants at work and whether asthma is better away
claims.quote: ask if there are allergens or irritants in the air at work or at home, and whether their asthma is better when they are away from these places.

claims.text: Occupational asthma: objective confirmation, referral without delay
claims.quote: The diagnosis must be confirmed with objective tests. The patient should be referred to a specialist (if available) without delay.

claims.text: Occupational asthma: exposure must be stopped immediately
claims.quote: The cause must be identified, and the patient's exposure to the cause must be stopped immediately.

claims.text: Severe exacerbation signs: talks in words, sits hunched forwards
claims.quote: Talks in words, sits hunched forwards, agitated

claims.text: PEF at or below 50% of predicted or best is a severe sign (citable summary)
claims.quote: PEF ≤50% predicted or best

claims.text: Drowsiness, confusion, silent chest are life-threatening and need intensive care
claims.quote: Transfer to intensive care if the patient is drowsy, confused, or has a silent chest.

claims.text: SMART is the preferred Step 3 and Step 4 therapy for ages 4 and older
claims.quote: In individuals aged 4 years and older, the preferred Step 3 (low-dose ICS) and Step 4 (medium-dose ICS) therapy is single-inhaler ICS-formoterol both daily and as needed.

claims.text: Recommendation for SMART in ages 4+ with moderate to severe persistent asthma
claims.quote: In individuals aged 4 years and older with moderate to severe persistent asthma, the Expert Panel recommends ICS-formoterol in a single inhaler used as both daily controller and reliever therapy

claims.text: Formoterol has a rapid onset
claims.quote: Formoterol has a rapid onset and a maximum total daily dose that allows it to be used more than twice daily.

claims.text: Maximum daily formoterol: 8 puffs (36 ug) ages 4-11, 12 puffs (54 ug) ages 12+
claims.quote: The maximum total daily dose of formoterol should not exceed 8 puffs (36 μg) for ages4 to11 years and12puffs (54 μg) for ages12 years and above.

claims.text: SMART reduced exacerbations 32% vs same-dose ICS-LABA plus SABA in ages 12+
claims.quote: For ages 12 years and above, the Expert Panel considered four blinded RCTsand two unblinded RCTsfor this question. Collectively, these RCTs demonstrated a 32% reduction in exacerbations with SMART(high certainty of evidence).

claims.text: Tiotropium Respimat was the only FDA-approved LAMA formulation for asthma at time of writing
claims.quote: At the time this report was written, tiotropium bromide (Respimat) was the only formulation of LAMA with US FDA approval for asthma treatment.

claims.text: Nearly 28 million people in the U.S. have asthma
claims.quote: Nearly 28 million people in the U.S. have asthma.

claims.text: 3,279 asthma deaths in 2024
claims.quote: In 2024, 3,279 people died from asthma.

claims.text: Nearly all asthma deaths are avoidable
claims.quote: Nearly all of these deaths are avoidable with the right treatment and care.

claims.text: Risk of death reduced by action plan, medicines, trigger reduction, medical help
claims.quote: you can reduce your risk of death by following your asthma action plans, taking asthma medicines as prescribed ... reducing exposure to your triggers, and getting medical help

claims.text: Emergency sign: color changes on skin, lips, fingertips

claims.text: Emergency sign: chest sucks in between neck, chest plate or ribs

claims.text: Current biologics list
claims.quote: The current biologics for severe asthma treatment include omalizumab (anti-IgE), mepolizumab and reslizumab (anti-IL-5), benralizumab (anti-IL-5 receptor), dupilumab (anti-IL-4/IL-13), and tezepelumab (anti-TSLP).

claims.text: Tezepelumab approved regardless of eosinophils, IgE, FeNO
claims.quote: Tezepelumab is approved for patients aged 12 years or older with severe asthma, regardless of their serum eosinophils, IgE, and FeNO levels.

claims.text: Tezepelumab particularly effective in type 2 asthma
claims.quote: Of note, although it is approved for non–type 2 patients, tezepelumab is particularly effective in severe type 2 asthma

claims.text: Tezepelumab upstream action
claims.quote: Considering its upstream inhibitory activity on the inflammatory cascade, tezepelumab inhibits the TSLP-mediated activation of dendritic cells and ILC2 cells

claims.text: Phenotyping and comorbidities guide biologic choice; dupilumab, mepolizumab, omalizumab approved for CRSwNP
claims.quote: patients should undergo proper phenotyping (T2-high or T2-low) ... Comorbidities should be carefully considered, and if possible, addressed with the same biologic. Dupilumab, mepolizumab, and omalizumab are also approved for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP)

claims.text: Response outcomes for biologics
claims.quote: The outcomes to evaluate are the reduction in systemic corticosteroid use, the reduction in exacerbations and healthcare use, and improvement in symptoms and lung function.

claims.text: EIB definition
claims.quote: Exercise-induced bronchoconstriction (EIB) describes acute airway narrowing that occurs as a result of exercise.

claims.text: Substantial proportion of asthma patients have EIB; may occur without known asthma
claims.quote: EIB occurs in a substantial proportion of patients with asthma, but may also occur in individuals without known asthma.

claims.text: Water and heat transfer out of lower airways
claims.quote: The epithelium may play a key role in sensing the transfer of water and heat out of the lower airways.

claims.text: Daily ICS or daily LTRA for symptoms despite pre-exercise SABA
claims.quote: For patients who continue to have symptoms of EIB despite the administration of a short-acting β(2)-agonist before exercise, strong recommendations were made for a daily inhaled corticosteroid, a daily leukotriene receptor antagonist

claims.text: Warm-up recommendation
claims.quote: For all patients with EIB, we recommend interval or combination warm-up exercise before planned exercise

claims.text: SABA typically 15 minutes before exercise; use less than daily
claims.quote: The inhaled SABA is typically administered 15 minutes before exercise. ... Such use should be less than daily, on average.

claims.text: SABA before exercise recommended for all EIB patients (FAQ)
claims.quote: A strong recommendation was made for using a short-acting β(2)-agonist before exercise in all patients with EIB.

claims.text: Cold, dry air in Nordic skiers
claims.quote: has been attributed to high ventilation inhalation of cold, dry air during training and competition

claims.text: Diagnostic criterion >=10% fall in FEV1
claims.quote: The criterion for the percent fall in FEV1 used to diagnose EIB is ≥10%.

claims.quote: allows categorization of disease as intermittent, persistent-mild, persistent-moderate, and persistent-severe. Initial treatment is guided by the disease-severity category.

claims.quote: ≤ 2 days per week | > 2 days per week, but not daily | Daily | Throughout the day

claims.text: Severity table: nighttime awakenings

claims.text: Green zone: no symptoms day or night, usual activities, peak flow 80% or more
claims.quote: No cough, wheeze, chest tightness, or shortness of breath during the day or night ... Can do usual activities ... (80 percent or more of my best peak flow)

claims.text: Yellow zone symptoms and 50-79% peak flow
claims.quote: Waking at night due to asthma, or ... Can do some, but not all, usual activities ... (50 to 79 percent of my best peak flow)

claims.text: Red zone description and less than 50% peak flow

claims.quote: Then call your doctor NOW. Go to the hospital or call an ambulance if: ... You are still in the red zone after 15 minutes AND ... You have not reached your doctor.

claims.text: Danger signs: trouble walking and talking; blue lips or fingernails
claims.quote: Trouble walking and talking due to shortness of breath ... Lips or fingernails are blue
